chapter: Cliff Jackson, Jelly Roll Morton and Harlem in the 1920s
title: Jelly Roll the composer and his last recording band
summary: Jelly Roll's compositions were advanced; Caldwell lists the New Orleans players on the last recording.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Well, also, I mean, he was undoubtedly -- I mean he was very -- I mean he had a lot on the ball as a composer, didn't he?
Those things he did were very good.
And I mean some of those early the way they were laid out records he did, I mean he (unintelligible), and that was very advanced for its time.

Very (unintelligible). You know, the saddest part about it, you know, the last recording we made practically all the fellows were with him (unintelligible) from New Orleans on that, Wellman Braud Becker Zotty (unintelligible), and it was Sidney Bechet, Albert Nicholas, Zutty Singleton. Then there was (unintelligible). Of course, he was from Indianapolis, him and his brother. They were from Indianapolis, Indiana, and Claude Jones, used to be with Duke. That's the last (unintelligible) requirements.
